objectives.title: Challenge 2: where the password is checked
objectives.prompt: Solve Hackademic Challenge 2. Where is the password actually checked: on the server or in the client? (one word)
hints: Read the page source: the form's button calls a script before anything reaches the server.

objectives.title: Challenge 3: name the weakness
objectives.prompt: Solve Hackademic Challenge 3. Which vulnerability class does it ask you to demonstrate?
hints: The page reflects what you submit back into its HTML.

objectives.title: Challenge 5: the checked header
objectives.prompt: Solve Hackademic Challenge 5. Which HTTP request header decides whether you get in? (header name)
hints: The page only welcomes a particular browser: what tells a server which browser you use?

objectives.title: Challenge 6: how the page hides its logic
objectives.prompt: Solve Hackademic Challenge 6. Which technique hides the page's real content from a quick look at the source? (name the technique)
hints: The source writes the page with a single script call over an unreadable string: decode it rather than reading it.

objectives.title: Challenge 10: the trusted field
objectives.prompt: Solve Hackademic Challenge 10. Which hidden form field does the server trust to decide whether you are let in? (field name)
hints: Look at every field the form sends, including the ones you cannot see on the page.

objectives.title: Fun with Frequencies: the technique
objectives.prompt: Solve the Fun with Frequencies challenge. Which classical cryptanalysis technique breaks its substitution cipher?
hints: Some letters are far more common than others in English text.

objectives.title: OTP Challenge: the mistake
objectives.prompt: Solve the OTP Challenge. Which mistake in the use of the one-time pad makes the ciphertexts breakable?
hints: Read the intercepted intelligence: what do all the ciphertexts have in common?

objectives.title: RSA Challenge I: factoring close primes
objectives.prompt: Solve RSA Challenge I (Bad Primes). Which factoring method is efficient when the two RSA primes are close to each other? (name)
hints: If p and q are close, N is close to a perfect square.

objectives.title: RSA Challenge II: shared modulus
objectives.prompt: Solve RSA Challenge II (Common Modulus). Which attack applies when the same message is encrypted under one modulus with two different public exponents? (name)
hints: Two coprime exponents and the extended Euclidean algorithm are enough.

objectives.title: RSA Challenge III: broadcast with e = 3
objectives.prompt: Solve RSA Challenge III (Low Encryption Exponent). The same message went to three recipients with e = 3: which theorem combines the three ciphertexts? (name)

objectives.title: Forging Signatures: the property
objectives.prompt: Solve the Forging Signatures challenge. Which property of textbook RSA lets a blinded message be signed and then unblinded? (name)
hints: Think about what happens to signatures when you multiply messages together.

objectives.title: RSA Challenge IV: small private exponent
objectives.prompt: Solve RSA Challenge IV (Small Private Key Exponents). Which attack recovers a too small private exponent from the public key alone? (name)
hints: It uses the continued fraction expansion of e/N.
